correctness.rationale: For every 0<a<1 and N>=2, the positive Poisson angular density yields E U=(a,0) with bounded unit observations and finite variance 1-a². The initial residual support forces the first averaged row, giving x1=v_N/||v_N||². For N=1 the unit row gives exact finite MSE a^{-2}-1. Antipodal cancellation for N=2 provides probability at least c r of a radius-r near-zero mean; at all N>=3, two independent tangent columns at a regular polygon give a local C¹ diffeomorphism and probability at least c_N r². Tail integration proves infinite negative second moment and error MSE; the strong law proves a.s. consistency. Differential bound on stabilized T, Hoeffding and deterministic ridge bias yield explicit O_a(1/N) mean-square upper bound. `checks.py` passed finite algebra and numerical tests; these do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison with Algorithm 2, Assumption 4.1 and Theorem 4.1 of arXiv:2603.29372 isolates the currently unaccounted-for squared inverse averaged row norm in a full-rank, positive-mean observation family. The classical uniform planar random-walk negative-moment literature contains the singularity as a general phenomenon, and regularized block Kaczmarz is prior art, but none of the inspected primary statements or published-result summaries directly give this sharp batch-one versus every-N>=2, arbitrarily-low-noise, forced-greedy, full-rank application with one-step ridge rate. Priority remains qualified by broader inverse-moment/ratio literature.

value.rationale: The source RGRK-SA method promises noise reduction from repeated normalized coefficient observations. This exact full-rank SPD, arbitrarily-small-noise model isolates why averaging unit rows does not control inverse squared averaged-row norms, and proves a sharp risk discontinuity between one normalized observation (exact finite MSE a^{-2}-1) and every larger finite batch (infinite MSE), despite a.s. success as N tends to infinity. A matched stabilized first-step estimate supplies an actionable calibration condition. The distinction is mathematical and algorithm-specific, not a mere assertion of nonzero noise or numerical rarity. Scope is deliberately one step.
